leverage_rationale: The page-resident pending proposal and accept/reject decision are central to the interaction and cannot be replicated comparably well by a detached server MCP; shared geometry and state make WebMCP substantive.
leverage_evidence: propose_layout stages translucent ghosts in the page and waits for a human decision.

usability_note: The editor appears information-dense but the proposal review model is understandable.
red_flags: Referenced video frame sheets were unavailable at the specified paths, so visual claims about motion and end-to-end execution are unverified.
standouts: Strong human-in-the-loop WebMCP design with pending tool semantics.

advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP interaction concept with credible spatial use case and substantial claimed implementation detail.

one_line: A human control plane that previews, narrows, and guards consequential agent tool writes.
what_it_does: Forks state, records a proof of proposed writes, lets an operator edit the approved subset, replays under a rollback guard, and returns detailed receipts.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP page-local execution is the premise: the human already owning the live session can inspect and selectively approve the exact write set before commit, something a detached general agent or server MCP cannot provide comparably.
leverage_evidence: Video transcript describes a 27-shipment proposal narrowed to 20 with explicit refusals and re-planning.
Writes are run against a clone, proof-edited, then replayed against real state under rollback.
Transcript reports rollback when a tool writes a field absent from the proof.
execution_rationale: The submitted 161-second video transcript gives a coherent end-to-end freight workflow, partial approval, receipt semantics, rollback, and a second product reuse; frame sheets were not viewable, but transcript evidence is strong.
execution_evidence: Video facts report 161-second demo.
Transcript covers proposal, clone execution, selective approval, receipt, replan, and rollback.
About text specifies four tools and guarded write path.
impact_rationale: Human approval and rollback for agent actions address a real safety and accountability gap in freight and infrastructure operations.
impact_evidence: Transcript grounds the workflow in cancelled flights, 42 shipments, lithium batteries, duty-manager review, and traffic leads.
The system preserves operator accountability while retaining partial automation.
creativity_rationale: Selective approval of a tool call's individual writes, with proof-based replay and rollback, is a memorable and sophisticated interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Operator can keep 20 of 27 proposed changes instead of accepting or rejecting the call wholesale.
Same engine is shown as reusable across freight and edge-infrastructure products.
usability_note: The staged proof, changing counts, refusal IDs, and receipts make consequential actions legible to operators.
red_flags: Guard only covers tools using the guarded path; the submission explicitly notes bypassing tools are not covered.
standouts: Best evidence-backed human-in-the-loop safety pattern in the packet.
Partial approval and rollback are concrete rather than merely descriptive.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP leverage, strong demonstrated execution, consequential value, and an original control model.
